segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As many of you here today have worked in the hotel industry for some time, I'm sure you have experienced the problem of high staff turnover in your hotels.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Every hotel relies on having loyal and experienced members of staff who make sure that everything runs smoothly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If staff are constantly changing, it can make life difficult for everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But why do staff leave frequently in many hotels?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Of course, many hotel jobs, such as cleaning, are low-skilled and are not well-paid.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A lot of managers think it’s this and the long hours that are the main causes of high staff turnover - but what they don’t realise is that it’s the lack of training in many hotel jobs which is a huge factor.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, what kind of problems does a high turnover of staff cause?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, having to recruit new staff all the time can be very time-consuming, and managers may have to cover some duties while waiting for new staff to arrive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This means they don’t have time to think about less immediate problems such as how to improve their service.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When staff leave, it can also severely affect the colleagues they leave behind.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It has a negative effect on remaining staff, who may start to feel that they too should be thinking about leaving.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, what can be done to change this situation?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Firstly, managers should stop making basic errors which leave their staff feeling upset and resentful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When organising shifts, for example, make sure you never give certain staff preferential treatment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: All staff should be given some choice about when they work, and everyone should have to work some evening and weekend shifts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you treat staff fairly, they’ll be more likely to step in and help when extra staff are needed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Keeping staff happy has other tangible benefits for the business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Take the Dunwich Hotel as an example.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It had been experiencing a problem with staff complaints and in order to deal with this, invested in staff training and improved staff conditions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Not only did the level of complaints fall, but they also noticed a significant increase in the amount each customer spent during their stay.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They have now introduced a customer loyalty scheme which is going really well.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now I’d like to look at some ways you can reduce staff turnover in your hotels, and I’ll do this by giving some examples of hotels where I've done some training recently.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Sun Club received feedback which showed that staff thought managers didn’t value their opinions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They weren’t made to feel they were partners who were contributing to the success of the business as a whole.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This situation has changed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Junior staff at all levels are regularly invited to meetings where their ideas are welcomed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A year ago, The Portland recognised the need to invest in staff retention.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Their first step was to introduce a scheme for recognising talent amongst their employees.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The hope is that organising training for individuals with management potential will encourage them to stay with the business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At Bluewater, managers decided to recognise 50 high achievers from across the company’s huge hotel chain.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As a reward, they’re sent on an all-exoenses-paid trip abroad every year.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Fun is an important element in the trips, but there’s also the opportunity to learn something useful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This year’s trip included a visit to a brewery, where staff learned about the new beer that would be served in the hotel.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Pentlow Hotels identified that retention of junior reception staff was an issue.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In order to encourage them to see that working in a hotel could be worthwhile and rewarding, with good prospects, they introduced a management programme.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These staff were given additional responsibilities and the chance to work in various roles in the hotel.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Green Planet wanted to be seen as a caring employer.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To make life easier for staff, many of whom had childcare responsibilities, the hotel began issuing vouchers to help cover the cost of childcare.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Louise Marsh at The Amesbury has one of the best staff retention rates in the business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Since she joined the company, she has made a huge effort to achieve this by creating a co-operative and supportive environment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For her, the staff are part of a large family where everyone is valued.

instructions: Complete the original Cambridge IELTS listening questions below.
questions.source_text:
SECTION 2
Questions 11-20
REDUCING STAFF TURNOVER IN HOTELS
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 11
    Text: Many hotel managers are unaware that their staff often leave because of
    Options:
        a lack of training.
        long hours.
        low pay.
    Q Num: 12
    Text: What is the impact of high staff turnover on managers?
    Options:
        an increased workload.
        low morale.
        an inability to meet targets.
    Q Num: 13
    Text: What mistake should managers always avoid?
    Options:
        failing to treat staff equally.
        reorganising shifts without warning.
        neglecting to have enough staff during busy periods.
    Q Num: 14
    Text: What unexpected benefit did Dunwich Hotel notice after improving staff retention rates?
    Options:
        a fall in customer complaints.
        an increase in loyalty club membership.
        a rise in spending per customer.
Ways of reducing staff turnover
Which way of reducing staff turnover was used in each of the following hotels?

    Q Num: 16

    Text: Pentlow Hotels
    Q Num: 19
    Text: Green Planet
    Q Num: 20
    Text: The Amesbury

    Id: A
    Text: improving relationships and teamwork
    Id: B
    Text: offering incentives and financial benefits
    Id: C
